The Ubuntu runner built the Docker image, passed the official JSONL handshake, passed all 20 public Docker protocol cases (95 SQL statements), and uploaded result.json with passed=true.

The first version returned [[1], [1]] after delete and reinsert because DELETE bypassed equality-index removal. After routing DELETE through remove_row, the query returned [[1]] and UPDATE affected exactly 1 row.
SELECT -9007199254740993 AS value now parses as Literal::BigInt(-9007199254740993), preserving the full signed 64-bit value.
Before the fix, SELECT NULL was parsed as a column named NULL. The parser now rejects it directly with ErrorCategory::Unsupported, consistent with INSERT NULL handling.

70 tests passed with one ignored benchmark after adding JSONL forced-kill recovery, semantic invalid-vector errors, signed BIGINT projections, explicit NULL rejection, batched vector storage, and delete/reinsert plus failed-insert index/storage regressions.

After batching vector appends at row-batch and WAL-replay levels: rows=10000 dimensions=128 queries=1000 recall=1.000000 write=445.7862ms query=1.3043352s cache_bytes=6151232. The earlier same-machine run was write=484.4624ms query=1.2972755s.

Before the key precheck, ten rejected duplicate-vector inserts grew vectors.bin from 12 to 132 bytes. Insert keys are now checked before materializing vectors, so the rejected batch leaves the file length unchanged.

experiments.output: The image build, full Rust suite, official JSONL handshake, and all 20 public Docker protocol cases passed; the uploaded public result.json reported passed=true.

implemented: BIGINT, Unicode VARCHAR, and finite float32 VECTOR validation
bounded paged vector storage with LRU cache
AVX2 L2 kernel with scalar fallback
tradeoffs: ANN initially reuses exact scan to protect Recall@10.
DDL is rejected inside explicit transactions to avoid undocumented implicit-commit behavior.
The official JSONL protocol is implemented; legacy text output remains isolated behind an explicit option.

limitations: Vector payloads are paged, but scalar values and primary-key metadata are still held in memory.
The official hidden cases are unavailable; public protocol v4 passing does not prove every hidden case will pass.
The official performance baseline is unavailable, so local benchmark timings cannot be converted into a competition score.
